location_qualifier: Caen sector west of the Orne
source_locator: R591: p. 121-122, 122; R278: Einsatz und Unterstellung (7 and 9 July 1944 entries)
current_activity: 12th SS Panzer Division still in the front line at Caen after the bombing of 7 July; forced to give way, with heavy tank and gun losses (Operation Charnwood)
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 7 p. 121-122: the air bombardment of the evening of 7 July also fell on the 12th SS Panzer Division, "still not relieved from front-line defensive duty as had been hoped"; the division lost twenty medium tanks, several 88-mm. pieces and all its antitank guns and was "the division eventually was forced to give way"; on the evening of 8 July Rommel and Eberbach decided to prepare to evacuate Caen. The Lexikon der Wehrmacht 12. SS-Panzer-Division page has the same bombing on 7 July and the division moving behind the Orne into the south of Caen on 9 July. Location: the sector at Caen west of the Orne; the point is the dataset place Caen sector, with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: neither source gives a village for the division on 8 July. Relationship: the division stays in the I SS Panzer Corps relation CR0054. Context: Schramm, OKW war diary (p. 324-325): the directive of 7 July ordered, among other things, the freeing of the 12th SS Panzer Division from the line.

location_qualifier: southern part of Caen behind the Orne
source_locator: R278: Einsatz und Unterstellung (9 July 1944 entry); R591: p. 122
current_activity: 12th SS Panzer Division withdraws behind the Orne into the southern part of Caen as British and Canadian troops enter the city
notes: Event date: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 12. SS-Panzer-Division page: "Am 9. Juli setzte sich die Division hinter die Orne in den Südteil Caens ab"; Breakout and Pursuit ch. 7 p. 122: on the morning of 9 July British and Canadian troops entered Caen from the flanks and reached the Orne. Location: the southern part of Caen behind the Orne; the point is Caen, with a precision of 5 km. Location support: moderate: the Lexikon (one family) gives the place; the CMH gives the situation at Caen but not the division.

source_locator: R278: Einsatz und Unterstellung (11 July 1944 entry); R600: p. 191
current_activity: 12th SS Panzer Division relieved by the 272nd Infantry Division and sent to refit around Potigny, north of Falaise
notes: Event date: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 12. SS-Panzer-Division page: "Am 11. Juli übernahm die 272. Infanterie-Division die Stellungen de[r Division], die zur Auffrischung in den Raum Potigny nördlich von Falaise verlegt wurde"; Breakout and Pursuit ch. 10 p. 191 has the 12th SS Panzer Division "undergoing rehabilitation farther to the rear" in the reserve of the Caen sector in mid-July. Location: the refit area around Potigny; the point is the town, with a precision of 5 km. Location caveat: the same Lexikon page also has parts of the division sent to Évreux and Dreux on 11 July (a date that cannot be right for the Dreux fighting, which fell in August); only Potigny is used. Location support: moderate: one source family for the place, the CMH for the refit.

location_qualifier: corps sector; division place not stated
source_locator: R594: German list, I SS Panzer Corps
current_activity: 12th SS Panzer Division listed in the July 1944 order of battle as corps reserve of the I SS Panzer Corps
notes: Event date: Nafziger Collection 944BGAA (Opposing British and German Forces, Normandy Peninsula, July 1944): the 12th SS Panzer Division "Hitlerjugend" is listed under the I SS Panzer Corps as "Corps Reserve", with a footnote that the 1st SS Panzer Division was being relieved by the 272nd; the file gives no day, so 15 July is the middle of the month and an approximate date. Event definition: a month-level list of the corps of the division; compare the Lexikon row of the same group, which gives the LXXXVI Corps for July. The two may belong to different weeks of July (the division was ordered toward the 711th Division sector on 16 July, Schramm p. 325), but no source read says so. Location: the I SS Panzer Corps sector at Caen, the corps the file lists the division under; a representative point with a precision of 5 km. Location support fallback: fallback only; the file has no place for the division.

current_activity: 12th SS Panzer Division listed by the Lexikon for July 1944 under the LXXXVI Corps, Panzer Group West, Normandie
notes: Event date: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 12. SS-Panzer-Division page, table of 1944: July, corps LXXXVI, army Panzer Group West, army group B, place Normandie; the table has no day, so 15 July is the middle of the month and an approximate date. Event definition: a month-level list; compare the Nafziger row of the same group (I SS Panzer Corps, corps reserve). Location: the table gives only Normandie; the point is the dataset representative point for the Normandy front, with a precision of 50 km. Location approximate: region only; not a unit position.

location_qualifier: 711th Division sector north of Lisieux; move ordered, division not arrived
current_activity: order given on 16 July to move the 12th SS Panzer Division into the sector of the 711th Infantry Division on the Channel coast north of Lisieux
notes: Event date: Schramm, OKW war diary (p. 325): on 16 July Hitler considered the transfer of a fast formation, if possible the 12th SS Panzer Division, into the sector of the 711th Infantry Division necessary, because a new landing might be aimed at the 711th; the OB West objected by telephone but "der Befehl zur Verlegung der 12. SS-Pz.-Div. sei inzwischen gegeben"; Breakout and Pursuit ch. 10 p. 192: Kluge agreed to move the division to Lisieux. Event definition: the move order of 16 July, not an arrival; the division was recalled to the Goodwood sector on 18 July (see the next row). Location: Lisieux, the objective of the move; the point stands for the 711th Division sector north of Lisieux, with a precision of 25 km; the division was not there on the date. Objective check: the order was given on the date, the division had not arrived. Event support: high for the order (two independent sources), low for any position of the division.

source_locator: R278: Einsatz und Unterstellung (17 July 1944 entry)
current_activity: one Kampfgruppe of the 12th SS Panzer Division alerted and moved to the Maltot area to the 272nd Infantry Division
notes: Event date: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 12. SS-Panzer-Division page: "Bereits am 17. Juli wurde eine dieser Kampfgruppen alarmiert und in den Raum Maltot zur 272. Infanterie-Division verlegt" (two battalion-strength Kampfgruppes had been formed from the remains of the two SS Panzer Grenadier regiments). Location: the Maltot area; the point is the village, with a precision of 5 km. Location support: moderate: one source family. Context: the same day the rest of the division was moving toward Lisieux (Breakout and Pursuit ch. 10 p. 192; Schramm p. 325); the rows are two parts of one division.

location_qualifier: Kampfgruppe at Vimont; rest of the division position not stated
source_locator: R278: Einsatz und Unterstellung (18 July 1944 entry); R600: p. 193
current_activity: 12th SS Panzer Division, turned back from Lisieux, put in at the Goodwood sector; the second Kampfgruppe moved to Vimont to the 21st Panzer Division
notes: Event date: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 12. SS-Panzer-Division page: the second Kampfgruppe "einen Tag später in den Raum Vimont zur 21. Panzer-Division verlegt" (the day after 17 July); Breakout and Pursuit ch. 10 p. 193: "the 12th SS Panzer Division, which had turned back from Lisieux, [was] hardly sufficient to affect the situation" of 18 July. Location: Vimont, the place of the Kampfgruppe; the point is the village, with a precision of 5 km. Location support: moderate: the Lexikon gives the place, the CMH the recall. Event support: high for the recall (CMH), moderate for the Vimont move.

location_qualifier: Dives crossing between Chambois and St. Lambert
current_activity: 12th SS Panzer Division infantry group under Meyer crosses the Dives between Chambois and St. Lambert
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 550: in the early hours of 20 August Lt. Col. Hubert Meyer ordered the infantry group to move out; at daybreak it met tanks of the 1st SS Panzer Division preparing to attack through Chambois, and the infantry began to cross the river in small groups between Chambois and St. Lambert; Meyer, having crossed, led a group on foot toward the southern spur of Mt. Ormel; some motorized elements also escaped that afternoon. Location: the Dives between Chambois and St. Lambert; the point is the midpoint of the two places. Commander: Lieutenant Colonel Hubert Meyer, the division commander (ch. 27 p. 550). Relationship: the LXXXIV Corps had only remnants of the 12th SS Panzer Division under its command.
